routes.label: Divide the perimeter by their walking rates

question:
Jane can walk any distance in half the time it takes Hector to walk the same distance. They set off in opposite directions around the outside of the \(18\)-block area as shown. When they meet for the first time, they will be closest to

[Figure 1](figures/1995_AMC_8_Q11_question_fig1.svg)
solution:
Jane takes half as much time to walk the same distance, so she walks twice as fast as Hector. During their shared walking time, Jane therefore covers twice Hector's distance.

[Figure 1](figures/1995_AMC_8_Q11_question_fig1.svg)

The grid is 6 blocks wide and 3 blocks tall, so the outside route has length
\[
2(6+3)=18\text{ blocks}.
\]
Because they start together and walk in opposite directions, their distances add to one full perimeter at their first meeting. Their distances are in the ratio \(2:1\), so Hector walks one of three equal shares:
\[
18\div 3=6\text{ blocks}.
\]
From the indicated start, Hector walks 3 blocks right to \(E\), then 3 blocks up to \(D\). Thus they meet exactly at \(D\), and the answer is \(\boxed{\text{D}}\).

edges.reason: Describing rectangle and square properties presupposes recognizing which plane shapes those names designate.

Written columns support perimeter arithmetic with larger dimensions. Adding decomposed lengths mentally gives the same result even for two-digit sides, so Gemini's chosen calculation does not establish column-method necessity.
The perimeter formulas use rectangle opposite-side equality and square side equality to combine their boundary lengths.

Fraction division prepares ratio values with fractional terms. The target expressly permits a simple ratio, and a whole-number pair such as 6 to 3 needs only ordinary division; no fraction-by-fraction division is universal.
Simplifying a ratio can reduce arithmetic. Sharing 60 in the ratio 4 to 6 by ten equal units already gives 24 and 36, so the greatest-common-factor simplification procedure is optional preparation.

Both the unit-part and fraction-of-total methods read the given ratio as relative shares. Simplifying to lowest terms is optional, whereas this meaning is common to the methods. Root checked both endpoint-based reviews; each identifies the stated content or conditional method rather than a curriculum-order claim.
edges.scope: Understanding the ratio terms as relative part counts before allocating a total
